Industrialisation et fabrication de munitions navales téléopérées et prestations associées (phase candidature).
Les conflits actuels démontrent que les drones et les systèmes autonomes sont devenus des capacités déterminantes, évoluant à un rythme sans précédent. C’est pourquoi la DGA a pour objectif de transformer plus rapidement les innovations en capacités opérationnelles au profit des Forces. Ainsi, le Centre Expert Référent Drones et systèmes Autonomes Navals (CERDAN) a pour mission de piloter le passage à l’échelle depuis le prototypage étatique à une série déployable sur les bâtiments de la Marine Nationale. Dans ce contexte et dans le cadre du projet interne SMOKERS, les centres techniques de la DGA conçoivent rapidement des solutions au plus près du terrain et des besoins opérationnels. Leurs équipes ont conçu et testé des prototypes de drones navals munitions téléopérées (MNTO), et souhaitent confier à un industriel l’ajustement de la conception, la production d’un dossier de fabrication, la mise en place de l’outil industriel de production et une production à un rythme répondant aux besoins des forces en MNTO. Il est envisagé des séries d’environ 10 / an en temps de paix et une capacité de 50 drones par an en fonction de l’évolution du contexte géopolitique. La présente procédure répond au besoin d’externaliser l’industrialisation, la fabrication et la gestion de configurations de ces MNTO à partir du dossier de conception du prototype V1 fourni par la DGA. Les caractéristiques techniques actuelles d’une MNTO SMOKERS V1 sont : - Poids 500 kg ; dimension 5 m de long ; - Moyen SatCom, RF et caméra IR ; système embarqué - Autonomie > à 50 nautiques, et vitesse max 40 nœuds.

Informations sur le temps d'acheminement

Les tailles des fichiers sont exprimés usuellement en octets (ko ou Mo).

Les débits de bande passante sont exprimés usuellement en bits par seconde (kbps ou Mbps).

Un octet vaut 8 bits, cela signifie que pour télécharger un fichier d'1 Mo avec une bande passante effective de 128 kbps, il faut (1 000 000*8)/128 000= 62,5 secondes (estimation donnée à titre indicatif).

CfT: Procurement of a High-Precision Optical Ground Station (OGS) Telescope Unit for Uplink and Satellite Tracking

Tender submission deadline in (days/hours):

Title:
Procurement of a High-Precision Optical Ground Station (OGS) Telescope Unit for Uplink and Satellite Tracking
CfT CA Unique ID:
Evaluation Mechanism:
Most Economically Advantageous Tender (MEAT)
Allow different Evaluation Mechanism in the MC/SC:
Description:
The Contracting Authority is seeking tenders for the procurement of a High-Precision Optical Ground Station (OGS) Telescope Unit for Uplink and Satellite Tracking. This procurement is being undertaken as part of Phase 2 of Ireland's QCI project (TransEuroOGS), co-funded by the European Commission Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) and the Irish Department of Culture, Communications, and Sport. The successful tenderer will be required to design, manufacture, and deliver a turnkey telescope unit encompassing the mount, optics, and control software, complying with strict technical and spatial constraints. Key Technical Requirements: Optical Configuration: Ritchey-Chretien (RC) optical design, f/10 to f/12 system, with a clear aperture of at least 700 mm. Low central obstruction is required (30 percent or lower diameter linear obstruction preferred, maximum allowable 34 percent or lower). Optical Coatings and Power Handling: Broad-spectrum reflectivity covering both visible wavelengths and the 1550 nm C-Band NIR telecommunication spectrum, biased for optimal performance at 1550 nm. Reflectance at 1550 nm must be at least 95 percent (protected gold or equivalent high-efficiency NIR coating acceptable). The secondary mirror (M2) and main aperture must handle a high-power launch beam of maximum 40W continuous wave at 1550 nm across the aperture or annulus (power density less than 3300 W per square metre on the primary mirror). Focusing Path and Clear Aperture: Must feature at least one Nasmyth focus port (more preferred). The Nasmyth focus path must be completely free of refracting optical elements (100 percent reflective optics only, with removable optics as an allowable deviation). Clear aperture path through the Nasmyth axis must be at least 60 mm diameter to support downstream Adaptive Optics relay systems. Mount and Dynamic Tracking Specifications: Alt-Azimuth Direct-Drive or equivalent performance mount with low-latency tracking dynamics supporting Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite tracking, including high-elevation passes over Zenith. Minimum Azimuth Slew Rate must be at least 5 degrees per second (faster preferred). Pointing and tracking accuracy must be less than 8 to 10 arcsec RMS during dynamic LEO passes. Fastest tracking rate must exceed 1 degree per second with fine range control below this speed. Envelope and Enclosure Compatibility: Total vertical height must not exceed 3000 mm from the base to ensure dome clearance. Maximum radial swing clearance envelope must be at most 1470 mm. The axis of elevation pivot height must ensure clearance at all pointing directions, with the pivot axis positioned no more than 155 mm below the centre of the clearance envelope (or at the centre or higher). Full CAD models and opto-mechanical layout files are mandatory upon contract award. Software, Control Interface and API: Native integration with standard open-source astronomical communication protocols (INDI / INDIGO) or ASCOM / ALPACA frameworks. Open, fully documented network API adaptable to HTTP/REST or WebSocket interfaces for automated robotic control, telemetry, and scriptable trajectory loading. Ethernet data interface and DC power supply preferred. Delivery Constraint: Unit delivery must be completed within 3 to 4 months maximum from contract signature. Please refer to the detailed Technical Specification document for full technical specifications, compliance matrices, and contractual terms.

normalized.title: S3-CL-14 - ZERO DEBRIS LARGE PLATFORMS PHASE 2
normalized.description: This activity supports the evolution of European large (> 1 ton) LEO satellite platforms in line with ESA's Zero Debris objective by 2030. normalized.title: M-IND - INDUSTRIALISATION OF MID-SIZE PLATFORMS FOR LEO CONSTELLATIONS (SAR OPTICAL)
normalized.description: Multiple studies on "Industrialisation of mid-size platforms for LEO constellations in Earth Observation".  This activity is part of the "vertical axis" of the M-IND (Mid-size satellite INDustrialisation) initiative and it is intended for mid-size satellite integrators in order to support the scaling-up of the production of European mid-size satellite (100-500 kg) for Earth Observation applications with LEO constellations. It complements the "horizontal axis" of M-IND, where separate technology activities, mostly fundedunder GSTP, will support Equipment suppliers to modernise and industrialise Equipment for sub-systems in mid-size satellites.This activity will focus on the definition and establishment of credible industrialisation roadmaps covering production ramp-up of full mid-size satellites for Earth Observation, including supply chain strategies covering interchangeability and interoperability of sub-system from multiple suppliers, modular platform architectures including modernisation of capabilities like for example low latency communication via Intersatellite Links (ISL), suitability for several types of Earth Observation payloads, and sustainability aspectsfor zero debris mitigation at end of mission life and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). normalized.title: IMPLEMENTATION AND MANAGEMENT OF ESA BUSINESS INCUBATION CENTRE CYPRUS
normalized.description: The network of ESA Business Incubation Centers (ESA BICs) is the largest network of space incubators in Europe. The two main objectives of an ESA BICs are to:Support entrepreneurs with a space-based business idea;Create and grow clusters of space related start-ups across Europe. All the ESA BICs are managed by local incubators with experience in supporting start-ups. They have good connections with local industry, universities, research organisations, as well as relevant government agencies and investor communities. ESA BICs follow the ESA BIC Common Approach to business incubation. So far, the network of ESA BICs has supported more than 2000 start-ups. Cyprus recently completed the ESA-Cyprus Plan for European Cooperating State (PECS) programme and recognized that Spaceis not only an important domain of research and development, but one of the key pillars of modern economy. On the 17th of March 2026, Cyprus became an Associate Member of the European Space Agency (ESA). The seven-year agreement opens the way for Cyprus's participation in ESA's optional programmes. As such, the Cypriot delegation asked ESA to start the implementation of an ESA BIC in Cyprus, under the ACCESS optional programme, in order to promote and foster the creation of startups active in the Space sector.  The objective is to find and support 15 space-related incubatees over an active period of four years, with additional two years added to thecontract duration to support any incubatees until the end of the incubation program. Each selected incubatee shall be entitled to an incentive funding of at least 60kEUR.
